summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of recurrent arterial and venous thromboses, asplenia, COPD, and chronic pain presented with chest pain and was found to have a new aortic arch thrombus on CT imaging despite being on chronic enoxaparin therapy. He was admitted for evaluation and management, with vascular surgery deeming the clot too high-risk for intervention. Hematology recommended transitioning from a heparin drip to therapeutic enoxaparin, initiating aspirin, and increasing simvastatin to 40 mg daily. A repeat anti-Xa level confirmed therapeutic anticoagulation. The patient's pain was managed with oral oxycodone, and he was discharged home with close follow-up planned for hematology, repeat imaging in one month, and ultrasound evaluation of an incidental renal lesion. His chronic pain and prior narcotic contract violations were noted, with recommendations for long-term pain management.
